title: ripwire
brief: "The ripgrep of AI context" — a zero-dependency C++23 CLI plus MCP server that gives coding agents a ranked, deterministic map of any repo: blast radius, tests-to-run and quality deltas. From Red Hat's emerging-tech group.
details: Ripwire (redhat-et/ripwire, 2.4k stars) — "the ripgrep of AI context": a zero-dependency C++23 CLI plus MCP server for coding agents. Two jobs: find what you want without reading the repo (ranked, deterministic call graph — what to touch, what it breaks, which tests to run; signatures at 74.7% fewer bytes than bodies), and check what you built (blast radius, tests-to-run, quality deltas). The quality panel automates review judgments from published research — eleven quality kinds reporting only what got worse, forgotten co-changes, fields read/written, ambiguous name resolutions — built on 49 repositories and 71 papers (McCabe through 2026 preprints) documented in docs/LINEAGE.md. Its honesty contract is unusual: every guess is labelled, every loss published, known false-positive modes documented with what to run instead. A field report (from a Claude-orchestrated 20-agent engagement on a 1,500-file codebase) claims it halved research spend and turned quality hygiene into a per-task mechanical gate — presented as one engagement's report, not a controlled measurement. Apache-2.0.
